issue_context.title: Secret created in Upstream Repo instead of Current Repo
issue_context.body:
# CLI Feedback

When creating secrets, they were unexpectantly created in an Upstream repo.


```powershell
gh repo view
myrepo123/MyApp123

$Secret | gh secret set $SecretName

gh secret list

> AEU2_MY_Secret123  Updated 2021-09-15

gh secret list -R myrepo123/MyApp123

> 

gh secret list  -R upstream123/MyApp123

> AEU2_MY_Secret123  Updated 2021-11-05
```

So this means that when creating a secret I have to do the following ?

```powershell
$repo = git config --get remote.origin.url
$Secret | gh secret set $SecretName -R $repo
gh secret list -R $repo

> AEU2_MY_Secret123  Updated 2021-11-05
```

I would prefer it the secret was created in the Repo that I am currently in?!
comments:
Thanks @mislav 

> Like you pointed out, we should just default to the origin remote when setting secrets to remove this magic behavior which makes more sense for querying issues or pull requests.

Yes that makes the most sense, I haven't tested it very much, however I may not have access to upstream on a fork that I am working on anyway, I guess the secret creation may fail in that case?

Anyway, if this is a duplicate feel free to close as such. In the meantime, I will continue to use the workaround.

This is bad and should be resolved. It makes my CI create releases on the upstream repo where I don't want it because I am only testing it on my personal fork. This should not happen. It should default to origin I think and be an explicit option and documented on the help.

This is super confusing, and could cause serious security issues. I was creating secrets in my fork (on my personal fork), and the secrets got uploaded to the original repo (which belongs to my company).
As I'm using those secrets to deploy to Azure, it means that my company repo started to deploy automatically to my personal Azure account, which is bad in so many ways!

Thanks for the feedback, everyone. Since this is tripping up a lot of folks, I will re-label this as a bug so we can handle it accordingly.

To clarify: if you were operating from the context of a GitHub fork (e.g. either there is a single `origin` remote pointing to your fork or there are `upstream` and `origin` git remotes pointing to the parent repo and your fork, respectively), should the default for setting secrets and creating releases always be `origin`, unconditionally? Or should gh interactively ask you to choose once or each time? Finally, if you wanted to be able to pass a flag to switch between git remotes, how would you imagine the interface for this to be? thank you 🙇 

Note that right now you can use `gh secret set -R owner/repo ...` as a workaround.

Thank you @mislav - for me this should always be the origin by default (see my commit just above on my own project).
Then you can keep the `-R` option for people who need some customisation: I would basically keep this the way it is, and just change that the default is now the origin.

Thank you for everyone's patience while we discuss this. We decided to remove the "magic" repo resolution from `gh secret` set of commands in favor of the following behavior:

- The local repo has exactly 1 git remote: use the repo named by the git remote;
- The local repo has more than 1 git remote: **error out**, list the available repos, and force the user to use the `--repo` flag to specify exactly which repo they want to operate on.

We believe that such approach would eliminate ambiguity and make it hardly possible for a user to accidentally send secrets to the wrong repository.

@wingleung : open to revisiting this with @williammartin given that all the former GitHub CLI maintainers involved have left GitHub and moved onto other pursuits.

### Where is the actual bug?

Looking at https://github.com/cli/cli/issues/4688#issuecomment-1016708631, the following logic for resolving the base repository is blindly picking the first remote:

https://github.com/cli/cli/blob/4b077daf7e74dbe6bf933f69e220066e3a12e8b4/pkg/cmd/secret/set/set.go#L168-L197

https://github.com/cli/cli/blob/4b077daf7e74dbe6bf933f69e220066e3a12e8b4/pkg/cmd/factory/default.go#L47-L55

Rather than a change in `BaseRepoFunc` logic, this issue would need to check the number of remotes in both `gh variable set` and `gh secret set` as described.

another alternative could be to get the remote from the current branch

```console
➜ git rev-parse --abbrev-ref --symbolic-full-name @{u}
origin/add-remote-check-to-secret-and-variable
```

☝️  we now know the local branch is tracking `origin`

still kind of seems like magic so I'm leaning towards being more verbose and forcing the user to provide a `--repo` flag

> another alternative could be to get the remote from the current branch
> 
> ➜ git rev-parse --abbrev-ref --symbolic-full-name @{u}
> origin/add-remote-check-to-secret-and-variable
> ☝️ we now know the local branch is tracking `origin`
> 
> still kind of seems like magic so I'm leaning towards being more verbose and forcing the user to provide a `--repo` flag

I like the thinking outside of the box while recognizing its magical nature might clash with security concerns of setting secrets in the appropriate place ❤

🙏 come to think of it, handling secrets and variables is a repo specific thing, not a branch specific one. So depending on branches might not be a good idea here. Especially for cases where the user creates new local branches

## Acceptance Criteria

### `gh secret`

#### Single Git Remote
1. `gh repo create` a repo
1. `gh repo clone` the repo
1. `gh secret set` creates the secret in the cloned repo
1. `gh secret list` shows the secret
1. `gh secret delete` removes the secret from the cloned repo

#### Multiple Git Remotes (interactive, prompting)

1. `gh repo create` a repo
1. `gh repo fork` that repo
1. `gh repo clone` the fork
1. `gh secret set` prompts with both upstream and fork as options, the secret is created in the chosen one
1. `gh secret list` prompts with both upstream and fork as options, the secrets are listed from the chosen one
1. `gh secret delete` prompts with both upstream and fork as options, the secret is deleted in the chosen one

#### Multiple Git Remotes (non-interactive, no flag provided)

1. `gh repo create` a repo
1. `gh repo fork` that repo
1. `gh repo clone` the fork
1. `gh secret set` fails with a message that the repo must be disambiguated by providing the repo flag
1. `gh secret list` fails with a message that the repo must be disambiguated by providing the repo flag
1. `gh secret delete` fails with a message that the repo must be disambiguated by providing the repo flag

#### Multiple Git Remotes (flag provided)

1. `gh repo create` a repo
1. `gh repo fork` that repo
1. `gh repo clone` the fork
1. `gh secret set --repo <upstream/fork>` creates the secret in the upstream/fork respectively
1. `gh secret list  --repo <upstream/fork>` lists secrets from the upstream/fork respectively
1. `gh secret delete  --repo <upstream/fork>` deletes secret from the upstream/fork respectively

review_comments: Everything from this logic tracks for me.  My main question is whether situations where `gh repo set-default` has explicitly set a remote / base should just use it rather than falling back to the prompting logic 🤔

I was in doubt here, it would kind of feel like forced magic here. Yes, you might set the default but there could be another repo you want to create secrets on, then you need to remember to override with the `--repo` flag because there would be no way in interactive mode to switch repos once you have a `set-default` one. I thought being explicit and transparent to the user would be the safer bet here

First, I want to say thank you for taking security so seriously 🤗 at GitHub!  Our Engineering leader `@mph4` constantly says _"Raise your ✋ if you're on the Security team"_ and I always do.

> Yes, you might set the default but there could be another repo you want to create secrets on, then you need to remember to override with the --repo flag because there would be no way in interactive mode to switch repos once you have a set-default one.

[`gh repo set-default`](https://cli.github.com/manual/gh_repo_set-default) already states that it is used to determine the base repo for creating repository and environment secrets:

> This command sets the default remote repository to use when querying the GitHub API for the locally cloned repository.
> 
> gh uses the default repository for things like:
> 
> - viewing and creating pull requests
> - viewing and creating issues
> - viewing and creating releases
> - working with GitHub Actions
> - adding repository and environment secrets

I'm sympathetic to this concern, however I believe an expectation has been set that prompting when there is a base repo set is counter to this and is at the edge of shared responsibility.

oooh I see, thanks for explaining it to me, I should've seen it in the docs. Even if it would be counter intuitive for some, that would be for another discussion. Given the guidelines of `set-default` I completely agree we can just take the default remote and use that.
PR updated, I'll look into add tests soon!
Again, thank you for being intentional and being open to discussion! 🙇

@wingleung : reflecting on https://github.com/cli/cli/issues/4688#issuecomment-1016708631 versus the code here, I think the original approach of prompting the user regarding which remote to use feels like the right choice still, erring if they don't pick a remote or if they requested [no prompting](https://github.com/cli/cli/blob/e36d8f103d5e1fb3989d9d5aefdae36b01fb88d4/pkg/iostreams/iostreams.go#L250-L256).

This would mean we don't need users to provide `-R,--repo` override as the previous workaround involved.

### Other commands that handle remotes

https://github.com/cli/cli/blob/e36d8f103d5e1fb3989d9d5aefdae36b01fb88d4/pkg/cmd/codespace/create.go#L143-L155

https://github.com/cli/cli/blob/e36d8f103d5e1fb3989d9d5aefdae36b01fb88d4/pkg/cmd/extension/manager.go#L691-L716

https://github.com/cli/cli/blob/e36d8f103d5e1fb3989d9d5aefdae36b01fb88d4/pkg/cmd/pr/merge/merge.go#L403-L431

Gentle nudge on this @wingleung, don't want it to get stale.

@andyfeller if I read this correctly it's a breaking change for the following **non-interactive** script:

```
gh repo create org/repo
gh repo fork org/repo
gh repo clone me/fork <-- sets the default to org/repo
gh secret set FOO BAR
```

Previously this would have put the secret into upstream (the bug), but now it will error. Just want to make sure we are clear and can communicate this.

> @andyfeller if I read this correctly it's a breaking change for the following non-interactive script

@williammartin : yeah; if we need to fallback to prompting when in interactive mode and encounter 2+ remotes, then this will break in non-interactive scripts.

**Is there a different way you'd suggest for addressing this than than https://github.com/cli/cli/issues/4688#issuecomment-1016708631?**

The security concern on this one resonates with me strongly.  If we're accidentally causing users to set secrets and variables on the wrong repositories, then I think we should fail when it is ambiguous in non-interactive mode. 🤷

I can't see any way to avoid it being a breaking change while also helping our users avoid a footgun. I'm a bit concerned about how many people it might break though.

https://github.com/search?type=code&q=%22gh+secret+set%22

More than 1.7 public results, and any of these that are run non-interactively against forks will be broken.

I've been very busy at work so apologies for the late reply.

OK, so if I understand correctly, there are 3 flows we want to cover, 2 of which are already covered in this PR

### ✅ flow 1: command with 1 remote
just use that single remote and proceed with the code

### ✅ flow 2: command with multiple remotes in non-interactive mode
error out but provide documentation on how to force a remote with `--repo`.

> This would mean we don't need users to provide -R,--repo override as the previous workaround involved.

in this case we would still need to support `-R` and `--repo` overrides, otherwise non-interactive flow will get stuck, or am I not interpreting it correctly? 😅 

```bash
multiple remotes detected [upstream origin]. please specify which repo to use by providing the -R or --repo argument
```

**use cases**

- `gh secret set MYSECRET --body "$ENV_VALUE”`
- `gh variable set MYVARIABLE --body "$ENV_VALUE”`

### 🚫 flow 3: command with multiple remotes in interactive mode
show a prompt to select 1 remote repo from multiple available remote repos using a search prompt 

**use cases**

- `gh secret list`
- `gh secret set MYSECRET`
- `gh variable set MYVARIABLE`

Is that correct?

### Breaking changes

we could do a minor release to introduce a warning for the v2 cli and mention this would be a breaking change in v3? Meanwhile working on a v3 PR

nice to see how remotes are being handle in other places, maybe in another ticket it could be looked into on how to merge all those strategies into 1 helper function.

- default to `origin`, fallback to first remote 👉 https://github.com/cli/cli/blob/e36d8f103d5e1fb3989d9d5aefdae36b01fb88d4/pkg/cmd/extension/manager.go#L691-L716

- default remote set to configured `set-default` remote value with a fallback to the first remote and prompt for user input on which remote to pick 👉 https://github.com/cli/cli/blob/e36d8f103d5e1fb3989d9d5aefdae36b01fb88d4/pkg/cmd/codespace/create.go#L143-L174

just to prevent this PR from getting too big or out of scope, I'd suggest to do this in another ticket 😄

> I've been very busy at work so apologies for the late reply.

@wingleung : I just want to say you owe us no apology; thank you for yet again working to improve `gh` ❤️

I think this summarizes the changes adequately, yes:

> ✅ flow 1: command with 1 remote
> ✅ flow 2: command with multiple remotes in non-interactive mode
> 🚫 flow 3: command with multiple remotes in interactive mode

Along with the actual changes to the command, we will want to make sure to call this out in the release notes to explain the motivation and hopefully how this is a one-time issue for non-interactive situations.

https://github.com/cli/cli/pull/9083/commits/81e7ecdfc135854c2609f769c4b47251da80b78e added a prompt for interactive mode on following commands
- `gh secret set MYSECRET`
- `gh variable set MYVARIABLE`

the other `get`, `delete`, `list` commands don't seem to support interactive mode.
